components.name: Worksheet
components.purpose: Method frame (board Worksheet / old-feed LineInput): the student writes each calculation line and the engine checks it against the step's expected solution graph; the default for every 'calculer / montrer que' question.
components.student_action: type lines with the math keys and number tiles; tap an earlier line to fix it
components.engine_needs: src/method line chains (lineChain, exprLine, mutations) plus one new solution-graph template per 3se question type (continuity, limits, asymptotes, symmetry, derivative, sequences, dot product, determinants, complex forms, counting, statistics)
components.props_sketch: frame type 'lines': graph {template, params}, variables (x, n, m, t, a, b), tiles
components.extends_note: 3se lines need what the parser and line engine lack today: (1) complex numbers (constant i, NumberSystem for a + bi) for T2_CH04; (2) vectors / coordinate triples and dot products as line items (vec(AB)(2, -1, 2), u.v) for T2_CH01/05/06/07; (3) equation, inequality and equivalence lines (=, <, <=, <=>) and inequality chains (0 <= |wn - 3| <= 5/(n + 1)), with solution sets and 'k in Z' families; (4) partie entiere E(x); (5) parameters (m, a, b, k, t) judged on samples of the parameter too; (6) exact display of surds (2 sqrt 7, 6 sqrt 21 / 7) and multiples of pi

components.name: CardsPick
components.purpose: Method frame: pick one of 2-5 sentence cards giving the reason, rule or claim behind a step ('polynome donc continue', 'terme de plus haut degre', 'orthogonal a deux vecteurs non colineaires').
components.student_action: tap a card
components.engine_needs: card evaluators (src/method/cards.ts, claims.ts); new claim kinds per chapter
components.props_sketch: frame type 'cards': cards [{id, text}], evaluator

components.name: PlanCards
components.purpose: Method frame: order 3-5 plan cards of a multi-step argument (continuity on R: pieces then junction; existence then uniqueness; plan d'etude of a function).
components.student_action: order the cards, confirm
components.engine_needs: checkPlan (any order respecting what each card uses)
components.props_sketch: frame type 'plan': cards [{id, text, uses[]}]

components.name: StatementTap
components.purpose: Method frame: tap the word of the French statement that decides the method (avec / sans remise, simultanement, au moins, exactement, un seul, ni ... ni, par defaut).
components.student_action: tap a word in the statement
components.engine_needs: none (targets in content)
components.props_sketch: frame type 'read': sentence, targets

components.name: PredictReveal
components.purpose: Commit to a prediction (which draw is most favourable? the same door?) before the inner visual appears.
components.student_action: pick a prediction, then explore the revealed visual
components.engine_needs: none of its own (the inner component computes; the prediction is not graded)
components.props_sketch: prompt, options (2-4), reveal (inner spec), insight

components.name: CompareTwo
components.purpose: Two inner visuals stacked to compare (draws with vs without order; notes before vs after the affine change).
components.student_action: explore both inner visuals
components.engine_needs: none of its own
components.props_sketch: left, right (inner specs), leftLabel, rightLabel, insight

components.name: NumericTwin
components.purpose: Pick values for the letter(s) and see both sides of an identity agree before proving it (1 - f(x) = (x - 1)^2/(x^2 + 1), cos 3x = 4cos^3 x - 3cos x, f(x) = ax + b + c/(x - 2)).
components.student_action: tap values, compare both sides
components.engine_needs: safe parser evaluates both sides at each value (exists); exact values for pi-multiples and surds
components.props_sketch: symbols (1-2 letters), template, compare, values (numbers or 'pi/12', 'sqrt(2)')
components.extends_note: allow two symbols (a, b) for f(a) - f(b) = ..., an integer symbol n, and values given as safe-parser strings (pi/12, sqrt(2)) shown exactly

components.name: CounterexampleHunt
components.purpose: 'Try to break this claim': the student proposes x, n or a bound M against a 'for all' statement (f(x) <= 1, d(x) >= 2, tan x >= x, g has a maximum, (An) is bounded) and the engine says whether the claim survives or is broken (local max 1 beaten by f(4) = 17).
components.student_action: type or drag a trial value, submit tries, then pick 'holds' or 'fails'
components.engine_needs: claim = inequality between two content expressions on a domain, or 'has a maximum' / 'is bounded above'; exact evaluation at the tried value; the true answer known from the analysis / sequences engine (sup, max, limit) so the final pick is graded; for 'bounded above' the engine returns an n with An > M
components.props_sketch: claim {kind: le | ge | has_max | bounded_above, lhs, rhs, domain}, variable, maxTries, hintValues

components.name: PointOnCurve

components.student_action: tap points to split the cloud, place G, G1, G2, drag an x-value to read the estimate
components.engine_needs: statistics.ts: mean point, partial mean points, line through G1 G2 exact, G on the line, estimates; weights from a two-way table
components.props_sketch: points [{x, y, w}], axes, ask: mean_point | split | fit | estimate
